text:
lee (Docs): Hey team — opened a small PR that adds a dedicated canary rollout example for Dedicated pools, plus a TypeScript SDK snippet and a couple link fixes. Need infra + ops sanity check. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/1421

omar (Platform): nice. Which rollout pattern are you showing? traffic-split or phased DNS?

lee (Docs): traffic-split by route with a 5% canary shifting to 100% over 10 minutes if health metrics pass. Also a fallback recipe to switch to Hosted.

jin (Infra): sounds good. For the SDK snippet, prefer naming createPool param provisioningConfig (camelCase) and the attachModel call is attachModel({ poolId, modelId, pinned: true }). Also use kms_key_arn in examples.

lee (Docs): updated the TS snippet accordingly. Here's the snippet I added: 

```ts
import { InfraClient } from '@redwood/infra';
const client = new InfraClient();
const conf = { gpu_type: 'a100-80gb', min_capacity: 2, max_capacity: 8, burst_config: { enabled: true, max_burst: 4 }, kms_key_arn: 'arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd' } as const;
const pool = await client.createPool({ name: 'canary-pool', provisioningConfig: conf });
await client.attachModel({ poolId: pool.id, modelId: 'redwood/gptx:2026-05-10', pinned: true });
console.log(pool.id);
```

tara (SRE): ops notes: use p95 latency for the canary health check and require cooldown >= 60s between scale events. Clarify that canary traffic uses the pool's isolation settings and will respect KV cache locality.

lee (Docs): good call — changed health metric to p95 and added cooldown note. Also included explicit line: "Canary traffic inherits pool isolation: ephemeral KV caches and tenant GPU allocation remain isolated for canary requests."

omar (Platform): add a short paragraph about rollback triggers for the route controller: recommended default is failover if healthy_replicas < 66% for 3 minutes or GPU error_rate > 5% over 2 minutes.

lee (Docs): added rollback triggers. I also found two dead links to the pricing page and the SLA matrix in the checklist — fixed to /pricing/dedicated-reserved and updated the slug for the SLA heading.

zoe (Support): please add a migration checklist bullet: "Verify Redwood service principal has kms:Decrypt on the provided KMS key and run a sample encrypt/decrypt test." Customers trip on this.

lee (Docs): added the KMS test step and a short email template for customer-success. I also added a billing callout: "Burst minutes beyond committed throughput are pro-rated per minute and will appear in usage invoices."

jin (Infra): tiny HCL nit — provider expects kms_key_arn and burst_config block. Example HCL I recommend: 

```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "canary" {
  name         = "canary"
  gpu_type     = "a100-80gb"
  min_capacity = 2
  max_capacity = 8
  kms_key_arn  = "arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd"
  burst_config = { enabled = true, max_burst = 4 }
}
```

lee (Docs): swapped to kms_key_arn and burst_config. Anything else before I merge?

tara (SRE): one more: include a note that preemptible fallback can increase tail latency and recommend configuring a fallback route in the canary plan.

lee (Docs): added preemptible fallback note and a short SLO row: "Burst fallback: latency SLOs may be relaxed up to 30% during preemptible fallback; burst minutes are pro-rated per minute."

omar (Platform): Approved for infra wording.

zoe (Support): Approve customer-facing copy.

ci-bot: docs CI passed — https://ci.internal/builds/5321 :white_check_mark:

lee (Docs): Thanks all — merging now and will post the canary playbook to #customer-success with the SDK snippets. :rocket:
